title: Authenticity and verification duties on every out-of-state pathway
rule_summary: All three out-of-state pathways place a duty on the FILLING PHARMACIST, and they are not identical. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(c) it is the duty of the pharmacist filling a schedule III through VI out-of-state prescription TO DETERMINE, IN ACCORDANCE WITH PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS AND PERSONAL JUDGMENT, THAT THE PRESCRIPTION IS AUTHENTIC AND VALID; and, PROVIDED THE SUBSTANCE IS IN SCHEDULES III TO V INCLUSIVE, the pharmacist SHALL ALSO VERIFY THE PRESCRIPTION BY TELEPHONE OR OTHER MEANS. A schedule VI out-of-state prescription therefore carries the authenticity duty WITHOUT the separate telephone-verification duty. Under s. 18(d) a pharmacist filling an out-of-state NONNARCOTIC schedule II prescription SHALL determine authenticity and validity AND SHALL VERIFY the prescription by telephone or other means; s. 18(d1/2) imposes the same on the NARCOTIC schedule II route. On every one of these pathways A PHARMACIST SHALL NOT FILL A PRESCRIPTION FOR WHICH VERIFICATION CANNOT BE OBTAINED, and A PHARMACIST SHALL NOT BE HELD LIABLE FOR REFUSING to fill such a prescription PROVIDED DOCUMENTED GOOD FAITH EFFORTS were made to determine its authenticity and validity.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate applies the verification gate to the pathway actually in front of them. The gate is easy to attach to schedule III through V alone, when the nonnarcotic and narcotic schedule II routes each state it independently and schedule VI carries only the authenticity half.

exceptions: Schedule VI is the one out-of-state pathway carrying the authenticity duty without the telephone-verification duty, because s. 18(c) conditions verification on the substance being in schedules III to V.
The liability protection for refusing depends on documented good faith efforts, not on the refusal alone.
common_confusions: Reading verification as a schedule III through V feature and filling an out-of-state nonnarcotic schedule II prescription without it, when s. 18(d) states the duty independently.
Collapsing the authenticity determination and the telephone verification into one duty, when s. 18(c) separates them by schedule.
Assuming a pharmacist who refuses an unverifiable prescription is exposed; the statute protects the refusal where good faith efforts are documented.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(c), (d) and (d1/2) read verbatim in the current official publication on 2026-09-10.
